prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 3: leave the boosted-tree family entirely and fit a bagged, fully-grown forest — extra_trees with 1000 randomised trees, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=1, unlimited depth — on the same median-imputed, unscaled matrix so the change is attributable to the family swap alone. Extra-trees averages fully-grown, randomly-split trees, a variance-reduction ranking generator structurally unlike the sequential residual fitting of hist_gbdt and xgboost, and its averaged leaf votes produce a much finer-grained probability ranking than 400–682 boosted stages did. Class weight stays at default (recall 0.914 vs specificity 0.955 is a mild imbalance whose entire correction is inside cut_headroom 0.006), so the whole attempt is spent on the ranking axis. I will read roc_auc, pr_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against attempt 1's 0.9793 / 0.9601 / 0.9408: if the best-cut ceiling again lands in 0.934–0.941, the three families tried span the ranking this feature set supports and the 0.967 bar should be reported as unreachable rather than chased with further retuning.",
  "model_family": "bagging",
  "candidate_models": [
    "extra_trees",
    "random_forest"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "n_estimators": 1000,
    "min_samples_leaf": 1,
    "class_weight": null
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Model family changes from gbdt (attempt 1 hist_gbdt, attempt 2 xgboost) to bagging: extra_trees with 1000 unlimited-depth trees, min_samples_leaf=1, no early stopping and no internal holdout, so all 2,760 training rows are fitted (attempt 2 gave up 276 of them to early stopping). No learning rate, no sequential boosting, no l2<path> regularisation knobs. Preprocessing is deliberately identical to both prior attempts (median impute, no scaling, no missingness columns) and class_weight stays unset, so the only variable moved is the ranking generator itself. I chose extra_trees over the Critic's random_forest because it is the more distant point from boosted trees — random splits rather than optimal ones — which is where the larger ranking step is if one exists.",
  "rationale": "The Critic's evidence puts 87% of the 0.0377 shortfall on the ranking axis: cut_headroom is 0.0048–0.0060 across both attempts, and recall<path> are close enough that any class_weight move is bounded by that same tiny number. Regularising inside gbdt already failed to move the ranking (best-cut ceiling 0.9408 → 0.9341, paired Δ unresolvable), so another gbdt point is not a plan. The only lever the executor offers that changes the ranking is a different family, and the two remaining structurally distinct high-capacity options are bagging (extra_trees<path>) and kernel<path> Bagging is the right first pick here: spambase's 57 highly skewed sub-unit frequency columns with strong-corr markers (word_freq_remove, word_freq_your, word_freq_000, char_freq_$) reward axis-aligned threshold splits, which trees give natively without scaling, and averaging 1000 fully-grown randomised trees yields a fine-resolution probability ranking rather than the coarse staged one boosting produced. Cost is safe: prior tree fits took ~4.5 s of a 600 s budget and 1000 trees on 2,760×57 is well inside 2 GB. Honest expectation: published spambase results cluster near 0.95–0.96 accuracy, so 0.967 balanced_accuracy may exceed what these 57 columns support with no feature construction available; this attempt is the decisive test of that, since a third independent family landing at 0.934–0.941 best-cut establishes the ceiling rather than leaving it a guess.",

  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 3
}
